title: What is Cryptocurrency - Coinbase Crypto University
description:
Cryptocurrency's popularity has surged in recent years, but what is it, and how does it work? In this beginner-friendly video, we'll demystify the fundamentals of cryptocurrency. We'll begin by defining cryptocurrency and distinguishing it from traditional currency. Emphasizing that cryptocurrencies are digital forms of money with Bitcoin as the pioneer, we'll examine key attributes, including decentralization, security, and transparency. Moreover, we'll delve into the critical role of blockchain technology in ensuring the integrity of crypto transactions. Whether you're new to crypto or simply interested in understanding the basics, you'll gain a solid foundation in the fundamentals of cryptocurrency and be better equipped to navigate the world of digital currency.

asr.full_text: The Cryptocurrencies that Are Money Cryptocurrencies are a digital form of money. Like money, they enable people or companies to transact, do business or make trades with one another. Just like there are many different types of money like the dollar, euro or yen there are many different cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin was the first cryptocurrency ever created and it's the most well-known. It was created in 2008, by Satoshi Nakamoto. But no one knows who Satoshi is or even if Satoshi is one person or an entire group of people. Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies differ from traditional money in a few important ways. First cryptocurrencies are completely digital. There are no Bitcoin bills or coins like with traditional money. With cryptocurrencies, all transactions are recorded digitally on a blockchain. We'll explain how here in a moment. Second, cryptocurrencies are decentralized, which means no single person, company or government creates or manages it. Traditional money requires a central group, like a a bank or government to manage the amount of money in the world and keep track of every transaction to make sure everyone is telling the truth unlike traditional money cryptocurrencies don't need a central group because they use blockchain technology a blockchain is like a shared record book that keeps track of every single transaction that takes place that record book can't be changed and it's constantly reviewed by a network of computers all over the world having this peer-to-peer network validate every transaction creates trust so no central group is required. Third, cryptocurrencies are 24-7. The internet doesn't have working hours or days that it needs to be closed, so crypto is a lot faster and more flexible than traditional money. Isn't the internet cool? Finally, cryptocurrencies are secure and transparent Remember the blockchain we were talking about? Every cryptocurrency transaction gets logged in an open source public record book that is visible to everyone AKA the blockchain So no one can change their records Ever Every transaction that has ever been recorded that's ever occurred can be reviewed and validated
